exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal, urgent caesarean, elective caesarean)
outcome: Neonatal serum C-reactive protein (CRP) levels 6-8 hours after delivery
cohort: 440 newborns who underwent blood tests for suspected sepsis
finding: Neonatal serum CRP levels were significantly lower following elective caesarean deliveries compared to vaginal deliveries, suggesting a potential impact of delivery mode on neonatal inflammatory responses.
mod_finding: CRP concentrations in neonatal blood during the first 6-8 hours of life are higher following vaginal deliveries compared to elective caesarean deliveries.
